messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 PAGER: Elevated 5xx error rate on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (alert: generate-5xx-high). Current pager: maya (primary). Threshold crossed 03:12 UTC. CI: customer-facing API errors increasing ~18%.
maya (primary): on it. seeing spikes in the 1m rate. pulling logs now. ETA 10m. I'm primary until 06:00 UTC but heads-up I have an overlap gap from 05:30–06:00 (holiday shift)
noah: can take overlap 05:30–07:00 if needed, I have lighter calendar. will stand by for handoff. @maya please DM if you need full takeover.
sam: quick Q — is this an infra/networking issue or model worker OOM? any obvious logs?
maya (primary): logs show repeated 500s from model-worker-gw instances returning "kv-cache-missing" errors and backlog on worker queue. not OOM. suspect routing fallback misconfig after recent rollout.
lee: customer impact: dashboard shows failed requests from a handful of high-volume tenants (acct: acme-corp, acct: beta-inc). affecting latency and error budget. opened incident ticket INC-2026-439.
jeff: if routing fallback is the issue, we can flip traffic to the older variant for impacted routes. that buys time. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/generate-5xx
ops-bot: Deployed canary rollback requested by maya: `rollback service/model-router --to=2026-03-10-canary` (submitted). Waiting approval.
maya (primary): rolling back canary now. will monitor for 2m post-rollback. running check: `curl -sS -w "%{http_code}" -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` in loop.
sam: thumbs for rollback: :thumbsup: If rollback doesn't stabilize within 5m, consider routing to dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2 as temporary fallback (low latency but costs more).
noah: volunteer to run the fallback route if rollback fails. I can execute the routing change: `redwood route set --service generate --variant stable --region us-west-2`
maya (primary): rollback finished at 03:18 UTC. initial checks green for 30s, but a small spike recurred at 03:20. still trending down overall. continuing monitoring.
lee: I pushed an alert annotation to the incident ticket noting tenant impact and that we initiated rollback. pinged support for acme-corp SLA contact.
jeff: suggestion: mute noisy noisy per-instance alerts while we observe to avoid alert fatigue: `alert mute generate-5xx-high --scope instance --duration 15m` — will do if we see lots of ricocheting alerts.
maya (primary): agreed on mute, jeff go ahead. @noah hold on routing change unless I call it — want to see 10m of steady-state first. thanks for offering.
noah: ack. standing by.
sam: also added a quick smoke test in the p95 path for the webhook pipeline to detect regressions: `scripts/smoke/generate_smoke.sh --tenant=acme-corp` — recommend running every 2m.
maya (primary): running one now. smoke test passed at 03:26 UTC. error rate trending to baseline. I'll keep primary until 05:30 but need someone to cover 05:30–07:00 — @noah confirmed, will you mark oncall calendar?
noah: marking now. I'll be primary 05:30–07:00 for any lingering issues. please leave handoff note here if anything changes.
maya (primary): handoff note: rollback applied, monitoring, tenant contacts notified, runbook actions executed (rollback + smoke tests + muted instance alerts). If errors spike again, escalate to infra team and route traffic to stable variant. thanks everyone :heart:
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-439 update: status=monitoring, owners=[maya (primary), noah (temp primary 05:30–07:00)], timeline logged.
sam: nice quick coordination — saved customer impact. :clap:
jeff: +1. good job. closing watch after 07:05 pending no regressions.
